queries.query: We have a Flutter app for our hospital's patient-facing kiosk and mobile platform — it runs on wall-mounted Android tablets in waiting rooms, iPads carried by nurses, phones patients download it on, and a web version for desktop browsers. The codebase is in `health_portal/` and uses Riverpod. I need two things done together. First, redesign the main dashboard and appointment-booking flow so the layout adapts properly across all these form factors — the tablet kiosks should show a split-view with navigation rail, phones should collapse to bottom nav with stacked views, the web/desktop version needs a persistent sidebar with keyboard shortcuts and hover states, and we should handle foldable devices gracefully. Use `LayoutBuilder` and breakpoint-based adaptive patterns, and make sure touch targets, mouse interactions, and keyboard navigation all feel native on their respective platforms. Second, I want you to audit the entire application lifecycle — right now I'm worried we have problems with our initialization order (we spin up a Bluetooth beacon listener, an MQTT connection for real-time queue updates, and a local SQLite cache, and I suspect they race on cold start), our `dispose` and cleanup logic is inconsistent when the app gets killed or backgrounded on the kiosks, and we're not handling platform signals properly on the web version. We also recently added Kubernetes health checks for the backend-for-frontend layer that serves the web build, and I need you to verify our liveness and readiness probe configurations make sense. For the lifecycle audit, return structured findings with severity levels, file locations, estimated fix effort, and concrete recommendations. The whole thing needs to work reliably in a clinical environment where a crash or hung screen means patients miss their appointments.

We're building a React-based knowledge base app called "DevBrain" that has a notes section powered by MDX files in `content/notes/`. I need help with three things: (1) Set up the content pipeline for creating and managing MDX notes — each note should have frontmatter with title, tags, date, and a `published` boolean, and I need a helper that lists all notes, filters by tag, and sorts by date. Include an example note with embedded React components. (2) We have a Laravel backend API that serves note metadata and handles search/indexing — write comprehensive Pest tests covering the NoteController endpoints (index with tag filtering and pagination, show, store with validation, destroy with authorization), the NoteSearchService, and a feature test that verifies the full content sync pipeline from MDX file parsing to database persistence. Use factories, mocking for the filesystem interactions, and dataset providers for edge cases. (3) On the frontend, we have a `<NoteEditor>` React component where users can toggle favorites, adjust tag selections, and reorder notes in a custom list — the component currently has stale closure bugs because the onClick handlers capture old state. Refactor all the state updates (favorites set, selected tags array, and note ordering list) to use functional setState so the callbacks don't need to be recreated on every render and we stop getting stale values when rapid clicks happen.

Our platform "FreightPulse" is a logistics orchestration system built on 14 Go microservices (order intake, route optimization, carrier matching, billing, notifications, etc.) communicating over gRPC and Kafka. We've been struggling with two related problems. First, when a shipment request fails somewhere in the chain — say carrier-matching times out or the billing service returns a partial error — we have almost no way to trace what happened end-to-end; logs from different services don't correlate and we're basically grepping timestamps manually. I need you to design and implement a full distributed tracing layer: generate correlation IDs at the API gateway, propagate them through gRPC metadata and Kafka headers, create parent/child spans for each service hop, and emit structured trace data compatible with OpenTelemetry. Include the Go middleware/interceptors, a Kafka producer/consumer wrapper that injects and extracts trace context, and a helper package for creating child spans with baggage propagation. Second, once we have that observability infrastructure specced out, I want to build an internal AI-powered incident investigation tool — when an on-call engineer pastes a correlation ID, it pulls the full trace tree and feeds it to an LLM to summarize what went wrong and suggest fixes. For that LLM integration, I need you to craft a precise, structured system prompt that instructs the model on how to analyze distributed trace data: it should understand span hierarchies, latency breakdowns, error codes from our specific services, Kafka consumer lag signals, and gRPC status codes, then produce a root-cause summary with confidence levels and recommended remediation steps. The prompt needs to handle ambiguous traces (partial data, missing spans) gracefully and ask clarifying questions when the trace is inconclusive. Give me both the tracing infrastructure code and the optimized system prompt with an explanation of the prompt design choices you made.

Our "AquaFlow" water quality monitoring service has a Rust backend using Actix-web and sqlx against PostgreSQL, and I need two things done. First, the data access layer is a mess — raw SQL queries are scattered across handler functions with no retry logic or proper transaction management. I need you to refactor it into a clean repository pattern with a `MeasurementRepository` and `SensorRepository`, each supporting transactional writes and exponential backoff retries for transient DB failures. Second, we've been running weekly lab analyses on water samples and tracking results in markdown notebooks under `lab_notes/`. I need you to generate an integrated report from the notebooks in `lab_notes/week-22/` through `lab_notes/week-26/`, pulling in the latest sensor calibration drift stats from the database (which the new repositories should expose), and then export the final report to PDF using our `scripts/export_pdf.sh` pipeline. The report should include trend charts described in the notebooks and a summary table of anomalies flagged by our threshold rules.

I have the TMF641 Service Ordering API spec (TMF641-ServiceOrdering-v4.0.0.oas.yaml) and the TMF646 Appointment API spec (TMF646-AppointmentManagement-v4.0.0.oas.yaml). I need you to generate a complete MCP server that exposes both APIs as tools so our AI assistant can create service orders and schedule technician appointments in one conversation. Make sure the tool names follow a consistent `tmf{api_id}_{resource}_{operation}` convention, properly resolve all the `$ref` and `allOf` schemas (especially the nested `ServiceOrderItem` and `CalendarEventRef` structures), generate mock API servers for both so we can test end-to-end without hitting production, and wire up the `/hub` subscription endpoints so the MCP server can register for `ServiceOrderStateChangeEvent` and `AppointmentStatusChangeEvent` notifications and surface them as tool-accessible event streams.

Our interactive language-learning web app "LinguaPlay" needs some work across three areas simultaneously. First, we just added support for Japanese and need to update our `src/locales/en.json` translation file — add keys for the new "lesson.listening_exercise", "lesson.audio_replay_button", "lesson.pronunciation_score", and "feedback.audio_not_loaded" under the existing `lesson` and `feedback` sections, and remove the deprecated keys "lesson.old_tape_player" and "settings.legacy_audio_toggle" that were left over from the old audio system. Make sure the JSON formatting stays consistent with our existing 2-space indentation and sorted key order. Second, we're building the pronunciation practice module where learners hear a native speaker say a word, then record themselves repeating it. Using Tone.js, implement the audio playback system: load audio samples from our CDN (`/audio/{locale}/{word_id}.mp3`), schedule a 3-2-1 countdown tone sequence using the Transport timeline before playing each sample, add a "replay" button that re-triggers playback from the beginning, and handle graceful fallback with a chime sound if the audio file fails to load. The playback needs to sync with an animated waveform visualizer we already have hooked into Tone's FFT analyzer. Third, we haven't touched this codebase in about 8 months and I'm worried about technical debt — the original architect left the company, we've had three different contractors add features, and our test coverage is unknown. Can you do a thorough evaluation of the overall project health? Assess the frontend architecture (it's React 18 + TypeScript), flag any problematic patterns or dependency concerns, estimate how much refactoring we'd need before adding the next set of languages (Korean and Arabic with RTL support), and give me a prioritized action plan with effort estimates so I can present it to stakeholders next week.

We're building a multi-tenant SaaS platform for managing clinical trial data at `~/repos/trial-hub` (Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL). Right now every authenticated user can hit every endpoint, which is a non-starter for our compliance audit. I need you to design and implement a full RBAC system with these roles: `org_admin`, `principal_investigator`, `clinical_coordinator`, `data_monitor`, and `read_only_auditor`. Each role should have granular permissions scoped to specific resources — for example, `data_monitor` can view and export patient adverse-event records across all sites in their assigned study but cannot modify them, while `clinical_coordinator` can create/edit visit records only within their own site. `org_admin` manages role assignments and can create custom roles by composing individual permissions. Permissions should be stored in the database (not hard-coded), and the system needs a middleware/dependency that checks the caller's role + resource scope on every request. Also add an endpoint `GET /admin/roles/{role_id}/effective-permissions` that returns the fully resolved permission set including any inherited permissions from parent roles (roles should support single-level inheritance). Include Alembic migrations for the new tables (`roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `user_role_assignments` with site/study scope columns), seed data for the default roles, and pytest fixtures that verify permission boundaries — e.g., a coordinator from Site A gets a 403 when trying to edit a visit belonging to Site B.

We're running a microservices-based e-commerce platform on EKS and need to roll out a new version of our order-processing service (`order-svc`) across three namespaces: `staging`, `canary`, and `production`. The current deployment YAML is at `~/infra/k8s/order-svc/deployment.yaml` and it's pretty bare-bones — no resource requests/limits, no pod disruption budgets, no health checks, and the rolling update strategy is just the default. Can you revamp the entire deployment manifest with production-grade settings? Specifically I need: CPU/memory requests and limits based on our Prometheus metrics showing p95 usage of 250m CPU and 512Mi memory, liveness and readiness probes hitting the `/healthz` and `/ready` endpoints on port 8080, a PodDisruptionBudget ensuring at least 2 replicas are always available, a HorizontalPodAutoscaler scaling between 3-12 replicas targeting 70% CPU utilization, and a rolling update strategy with maxSurge of 25% and maxUnavailable of 0 so we get zero-downtime deploys. Also set up the corresponding Service and Ingress resources with proper annotations for our AWS ALB ingress controller. Once the manifests are ready, walk me through the exact `kubectl` commands to do a staged rollout — first to staging, validate with a smoke test, then push to canary with only 10% traffic weight, and finally promote to full production — including how to do an emergency rollback if the canary metrics look bad.
